name: How do I avoid uncovering expensive surprises mid-remodel?

mainEntity.name: What can be done before demolition to reduce the chance of hidden-condition surprises in an older home?
mainEntity.text: What can be done before demolition to reduce the chance of hidden-condition surprises in an older home?

acceptedAnswer.text: You cannot remove all uncertainty from an older-home remodel, but you can dramatically reduce it. The best protection is a preconstruction process that looks beyond finishes. That should include inspections of structure, roofing, plumbing, electrical, drainage, and any areas that show stains, cracking, or prior patching. If needed, open selected test areas so the team can see what is actually behind walls and under floors. Engineering review is especially helpful when wall removal, additions, or seismic upgrades are possible. Early utility evaluation also matters because panel capacity, pipe condition, and ventilation often affect the whole project. Most importantly, the budget should include contingency for the issues that are most likely to appear. That does not mean expecting disaster; it means planning like an older house will reveal at least one expensive truth.
acceptedAnswer.description: A thorough preconstruction inspection, targeted opening of suspect areas, engineering review, and early utility evaluation can reduce surprises. You cannot eliminate unknowns in an older home, but you can find the biggest risks before construction starts and build a contingency into the plan.
